lots.guide_summary: All surviving close entries are SOLD Gowans hammers for full-size walnut slabs, Jun to Oct 2026: $50 to $135 hammer (most $55 to $95; the best visual match made $85 on 2026-10-04). No UNSOLD or ASKING entries survive. Myrtle and macrocarpa slabs at $110 to $125 are context only. All AUD, no FX.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving full-size walnut slab SOLD = $50 hammer (lot 434906, Aug 2026) / 1.198 = $41.7, round down to $40 (all-in $47.92). Flip: likely resale at Gowans about $85 hammer (best visual match 442917 and median of the wider, paler slabs) less about 15% seller commission ($12.75) = $72.25, no outbound postage (local pickup, slab too big to post) = $72.25 / 2.396 = $30.15, round down to $30. Buyer's premium 19.8%, inbound freight $0. If you want it for a project, paying up to the $85 hammer that the best match made is defensible, but that is above the formal keep maximum.
lots.confidence_reason: Species rests on the Gowans title, but the colour and figure match recent Gowans 'SLAB OF WALNUT' lots from the same shed (especially 442917), and there are ten opened SOLD results. No mark applies to timber; size, thickness, moisture and cracks are not confirmed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Chalk '1404 16/10/26' on the face. Pale cream to light brown timber with dark swirling cathedral and olive-like figure, one knot near mid-height, a darker spalt or stain zone at the base, live edge on the left, rough-sawn face. Some checking at the top end. Not dark black-walnut colour, but it matches the pale English walnut slabs Gowans has sold this year.
lots.condition: Raw, unfinished, rough sawn. Some end checks visible at the top; thickness and dryness unknown.
lots.question_for_gowans: What are the length, width and thickness of lot 1404, is it air dried, and are there any through-cracks or splits beyond the top end checks?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Gowans 418737 'PIECE OF WALNUT' $20 and 417132 'PIECE OF WALNUT WOOD' $35 (photos show short offcut blocks, not a full slab, so not comparable despite the title). Dropped: The Lumber Shack US$1,133.97 and Etsy US$165/US$350 (snippet only, never opened, overseas kiln-dried and surfaced retail stock, so not comparable; the researcher's AUD rate was assumed, not looked up). Researcher's myrtle and macrocarpa entries kept as category guide only, not in the range.

lots.guide_summary: Nothing same-item or close survives. Context only: Gowans pairs of retro or leather armchairs of other styles made $35 to $300 hammer (SOLD, category guide), and a US dealer asked US$3,000 (about A$4,298) for a restored IKEA pine and patchwork pair with different arms (ASKING, category guide). No UNSOLD evidence.
lots.working: No same-item or close SOLD evidence, so both maximums are 0. Indicative only: Gowans buyers pay about $150 to $300 hammer for a decent matching retro or leather pair; with one seat cushion patched and worn arm finish, about $100 to $200 hammer ($120 to $240 all-in at 19.8%) looks realistic unless a Scandinavian maker label turns up.
lots.confidence_reason: No label or mark visible, design attribution is a guess, and the only evidence is category-guide sales and one overseas dealer asking price for a different model.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Dark-stained solid timber frames with broad flat paddle arms and visible finish wear on the arm tops. Tan to cognac patchwork leather cushions, button tufted; the left chair's seat has a darker brown patch strip (repair or replacement panel). Leather has creasing but no obvious tears in the photo. No maker label visible.
lots.condition: Used. Worn finish on arms, one seat cushion with a darker repair strip, general leather creasing. Webbing or springs not visible.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there a maker's label or stamp under the seats or on the frames of lot 1492 (for example a Swedish, Norwegian or Danish maker or IKEA)? Is the leather sound, is the darker strip a repair, and are the seat supports (straps or springs) intact?

lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD = $140 hammer (lot 384459, Jan 2026) / 1.198 = $116.9, round down to $115 (all-in $137.77). Flip: likely resale about $150 hammer at Gowans (midpoint of the two close sales) less about 15% seller commission ($22.50) = $127.50, no outbound postage (local pickup) = $127.50 / 2.396 = $53.2, round down to $50. Buyer's premium 19.8%, inbound freight $0. Rests on only two close sales of different form, so treat $115 as a ceiling, not a target.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear photos of an honest mid-century two door cabinet with no label, and two close but not identical Gowans SOLD results opened via the API. Only two entries and no maker.
lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos. Golden figured veneer or ply doors with small pins visible around the door edges and a few marks and a faint stain on the right door; solid timber top with minor wear; single carved pull spanning both doors; tapered legs with brass ferrules (one rear leg looks a slightly different tone). Inside: one full-width shelf on a central support, plain solid softwood interior, doors are plain ply inside. No label or stamp visible.
lots.condition: Good used. Light surface wear and small marks on doors and top, no obvious veneer lifting or broken hinges in the photos.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there any maker's label or stamp on the back or inside of lot 1495, what are its dimensions, and are the legs original and the doors closing square?
